Scope and evidence

All eight changed diff sections were reviewed: crates/daemon/src/community/root.rs, crates/daemon/src/http/shim.rs, crates/daemon/src/pa_presence.rs, crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs, crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog_tests.rs, crates/daemon/tests/presence_launches.rs, docs/difficulties.md and docs/how/pa-watchdog.md. The security source inspection was delegated once; this role holder independently verified finality, exact-head CI/JUnit evidence and the live baseline. The report's retained source receipts were obtained before publication.

- community/root.rs:200-241,266-267 uses finite ancestors traversal and follows one gitdir pointer and one commondir pointer, not a recursive pointer graph. A regular .git file pointing to itself reaches the directory check and becomes Unknown. A commondir cycle is not recursively followed, although an existing directory is not fully validated as Git metadata. Paths are canonicalized and may resolve outside the checkout; containment is not an authorization boundary under C33.
- http/mod.rs:438-451,754-795 retains bearer middleware and peer-key restrictions. registration.rs:1078-1084,1190 retains folder admission. No new endpoint, credential, privilege or network destination is introduced. No outside-account path to unauthorized access, disclosure or execution was established.
- pa_watchdog.rs:1110-1175 launches git only for Unknown, through the existing program resolver and separate arguments (-C, folder, rev-parse, --path-format=absolute, --git-common-dir), not a shell string. -C selects Git's repository context; the code does not set the child process cwd to the folder. The existing resolver is not an unconditional absolute-path guarantee for user-configured relative PATH entries; that behavior is unchanged and the live resolver result was not probed. The two-second timeout and kill_on_drop remain; spawns::record("git.pa-watchdog-common-dir") remains immediately before the fallback launch at line 1150. Placement is read before the ten-minute fallback cache.
- http/shim.rs:96-133 retains JSON response shape, live filtering, per-request folder deduplication and fallback-to-folder. Normal checkout/worktree discovery is shared; malformed-layout behavior is not universally identical.
- Both changed documents were inspected in full. Added receipt text at docs/difficulties.md:154 and docs/how/pa-watchdog.md:111-113 revealed no identified credentials, private repository coordinates or machine-specific home paths. Direct pure scanText checks found zero home-path findings in all eight files; the normal operational scanner excludes these files, so that scoped scan is not a claim that the full repository gate ran successfully. No manifest, lockfile, workflow or notes-push changes appear. No credentials or refs/notes contents were read; no push was performed.

Nonblocking operational limits

community/root.rs:219,225 uses synchronous read_to_string without a byte cap, regular-file requirement or filesystem-read timeout. A FIFO/device-backed or oversized metadata file can therefore block or consume resources before the Git timeout applies. The shim now shares this reader rather than its old .git.is_file() gate. This is a source-derived operational-hardening observation: no synthetic FIFO/device/oversized probe or normal-use harmful hang was demonstrated, and no added outside-account exploit path was established. Under C33/C34 it is not a security block. "Small reads" describes expected ordinary metadata, not an enforced bound.

Placement is POLICY, not a brake: its key selects the PA/prime receiving a seat's wakes. The existing 60-second round now does in-process filesystem work at placement calls, including the per-PA x live-seat paths (pa_watchdog.rs:514-515,975-987), plus presence/tombstoned-PA reads (pa_presence.rs:1121-1126). Those paths scale with PA count x seat count x ancestor depth, not merely distinct folders. There is no new timer or launch site. The former boot/new-folder Git burst is removed for decided layouts; Unknown fallback is at most one Git launch per folder per 600 seconds. Zero launches alone does not prove bounded filesystem latency. This is not a substitute for the performance role's verdict.

Independently verified proof

- just pr-freeze 248: FINAL at the full head above, clean detached worktree, base main, CLEAN merge state and all five latest CI checks successful.
- CI run 44434863733, rust-test job 135261066747, Ubuntu 24.04, exact requested head: cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci passed 2,516 tests; six tests were excluded/skipped by the run. Artifact 14488941754 was selected from that successful job's upload log, not by artifact name alone. Its JUnit contains passing, non-skipped entries for place_names_the_common_dir_git_names, place_leaves_what_it_cannot_read_to_git, a_recreated_worktree_is_placed_in_its_new_repository_at_once, the_presence_checks_and_placing_folders_launch_nothing and shim_sessions_emits_the_frozen_legacy_names_and_resolves_git_common_dir, plus all six pij-testkit::spawn_sites tests.
- 2026-11-19 01:17:35Z to 01:17:55Z, running PRE-CHANGE daemon 8863651685: uptime 23:57 to 24:17; git.pa-watchdog-common-dir 28 to 28; total daemon launches 781 to 781. just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json completed: 128.8 whole-machine launches/s; no daemon children sampled (sampling attribution is only a lower bound). /bin/ps snapshots: CPU 15.4% to 13.0%, RSS 147872 to 146704 KiB; these are snapshots, not a controlled CPU comparison.
- harness boot --json: advisory ready:false before TypeScript stages because worktree dependencies are absent. harness checks --quick --json: exit 1; seven tooling-dependent stages failed from missing dependencies or an ambient Biome mismatch, while pij-skill and copilot-native passed. Rust, route-inventory and smoke were skipped. This is NOT a green local gate.

Proof limits and owed work

No local Cargo build/test, dependency installation/link, daemon bounce/deploy, credential-file read or code edit was performed. Linux CI is not macOS execution proof. The actual checkout's ordinary worktree metadata was compared with Git during source review; adversarial runtime metadata fixtures were not executed. The after-merge/bounce readings at boot and again after more than ten minutes remain owed to the merger/performance owner; this pre-change 20-second baseline cannot prove the changed daemon's behavior or a ten-minute retry rate.

Harness feedback retained for the close/memory turn: a dependency-free review-proof command should collect finality, successful-job artifact identity, named JUnit outcomes and sanitized timed runtime receipts without invoking builds or falling through to ambient tooling.
